scope: Exact eight repository implementation/pin/test-registration/specification leaves and seven decoded Go outputs, under serialized texture/frame ownership.

invariants: Texture publication admits a complete live owned texture/view pair and retires failed/partial creation references. Empty borrowed retirement clears shared state; created pairs explicitly publish owned mode.

Reuse requires live device/queue, live owned same-origin texture/view, exact format and all requested usage bits. Image/render transitions replace incompatible resources; SetFromGoImage also rejects an invalid/missing pair rather than uploading through a format-only shortcut.

Explicit device/queue changes retire texture/view/sampler/staging. Same-device staging allocation refusal preserves old buffer/dimensions; successful replacement explicitly releases the previous reference instead of relying on GC.

Four-byte single-layer resolve layout validates positive dimensions, uint32 row/image limits and Go map length before allocating/mapping. Checked copy and stale/missing read admission preserve existing explicit configuration/copy/submission preconditions.

Raw ReadData remains native channel order; ReadGoImage normalizes detached BGRA bytes to NRGBA without changing alpha/transfer bytes. GrabImage refuses a failed copy/read while completing an otherwise valid render.

NoDisplayGPU refuses a nil adapter before NewDevice. createHeadlessPair cleans returned partial device then GPU references on ordinary nil/error admission; it leaves shared global Instance ownership with final shutdown.
fixture_review: The explicit VELLUM_TEXTURE_GPU_TEST=1 gate and !js build constraint keep the tiny real-GPU fixture out of ordinary execution. It creates no application window, surface or presentation path and records no performance/physical-memory metric.

Guarded device/GPU/Instance teardown is installed before calling NoDisplayGPU, so missing-adapter or device-error termination cannot skip fixture cleanup. Each successful subtest installs its texture/device/command-buffer cleanup before subsequent failure checks.

Image↔render usage checks strongly retain the old texture wrappers and require their explicit invalidation. Staging checks retain all32 old buffer wrappers, assert immediate owner-reference retirement/reuse and perform idempotent final cleanup. Device-change checks retire old texture/view/staging before allocating new staging.

Two3x2RGBA/BGRA transfer cases check exact unpadded native-order bytes, padded copy/map dimensions and detached normalized image bytes after queue submission/mapping. They cover tiny transfer/reference correctness, not physical heap reclamation or general GPU fault recovery.

The five-case injected headless admission table verifies missing adapter, device error, partial device, nil-without-error and success, with exact cleanup order/error identity. Defensive partial-handle tables remain separate from pinned native factory behavior.

resolved_findings.resolution: Device/queue change invalidates staging ownership before same-sized reuse.
Detached ReadGoImage normalizes BGRA; raw ReadData remains native order.
Empty borrowed retirement unconditionally clears shared mode; created pairs explicitly own their handles.
Same-format shortcuts require a live device and queue.

Fixture teardown is registered before NoDisplayGPU; missing-adapter admission is checked and returned failed/partial device admission releases GPU ownership without releasing the shared global Instance.
